quests.partialSentence: Could you tell me where ____?
quests.hint: In polite indirect questions the word order is normal.
quests.explanation: After 'Could you tell me', use statement order: 'where the station is'.

quests.partialSentence: Do you know what time ____ tomorrow?
quests.hint: Indirect questions do not use the auxiliary.
quests.explanation: Indirect questions use statement order without do/does.

quests.partialSentence: I'd like to know how much ____.
quests.explanation: Word order returns to normal in indirect questions.

quests.partialSentence: The company ____ finally replied to my application.
quests.hint: The preposition stays with the verb.
quests.explanation: In relative clauses the preposition often comes at the end: 'I applied to'.

quests.partialSentence: Is this the person ____?
quests.hint: The clause is a relative clause.
quests.explanation: Word order in relative clauses is subject + verb + preposition.

quests.partialSentence: The hotel ____ was fully booked.
options: at we had hoped to stay
we had hoped to stay at
quests.correctAnswer: we had hoped to stay at
quests.hint: The clause needs the correct preposition.
quests.explanation: The relative clause keeps 'stay at' together.

quests.partialSentence: I don't remember where ____ my keys.
quests.hint: The clause is embedded in a statement.
quests.explanation: Embedded questions use statement order.

quests.partialSentence: She asked me why ____ so quiet.
quests.explanation: The verb follows the subject in embedded questions.

quests.partialSentence: Nobody understands how ____.
quests.explanation: Statement order is used.

quests.partialSentence: The instructions were ____ confusing that nobody could assemble the shelf.
quests.explanation: 'So' + adjective + 'that' shows result.

quests.partialSentence: It was ____ a strong wind that several trees fell down.
quests.hint: The pattern here includes the article 'a' before the adjective and noun.
quests.explanation: 'Such a' + adjective + noun + 'that' shows result.

quests.partialSentence: There was so much traffic ____ we missed the ferry.
quests.explanation: 'So much ... that' introduces the result.

quests.partialSentence: If I ____ more free time, I would take a pottery class.
quests.explanation: Second conditional uses past simple in the if-clause.

quests.partialSentence: If she ____ our address, she would send a card.
quests.explanation: Past simple shows an unreal present.

quests.partialSentence: What would you do if you ____ the lottery?
quests.explanation: Past simple in the if-clause.

quests.partialSentence: The longer you wait, ____ the tickets will be.
quests.hint: The sentence uses a paired structure.
quests.explanation: 'The + comparative, the + comparative' shows parallel change.

quests.partialSentence: The film was much better ____ I had expected.
quests.hint: Comparatives like 'better' need a specific linking word before the comparison clause.
quests.explanation: 'Than' introduces the compared clause.

quests.partialSentence: He isn't as patient ____ his brother is.
quests.explanation: 'As...as' compares equal qualities.

quests.partialSentence: We left early ____ we could beat the traffic.
quests.explanation: 'So that' introduces purpose.

quests.partialSentence: ____ the road is repaired, buses will use the old route.
quests.explanation: 'Until' marks the end point.

quests.partialSentence: The instructions were clear; ____, several people made mistakes.
quests.explanation: 'Nevertheless' signals contrast.

quests.partialSentence: The customer to ____ I sent the quotation hasn't replied.
quests.hint: A formal preposition comes before the pronoun.
quests.explanation: After a preposition, formal English uses 'whom'.

quests.partialSentence: This is the book about ____ I was telling you.
quests.hint: A preposition comes before the pronoun.
quests.explanation: After a preposition, 'which' is used for things.

quests.partialSentence: She's the only one ____ knows the password.
quests.explanation: 'Who' is the subject form for people.

quests.partialSentence: Even though we had booked months ahead, ____.
options: the hotel having no record of our reservation
the hotel had no record of our reservation
but the hotel had no record of our reservation
yet the hotel had no record of our reservation
quests.correctAnswer: the hotel had no record of our reservation
quests.hint: The first clause already carries the contrast.
quests.explanation: With 'even though', don't add 'but' or 'yet'. The main clause follows directly.

quests.partialSentence: Because the printer was out of ink, ____.
options: so we emailed the document instead
and so we emailed the document instead
that we emailed the document instead
quests.explanation: 'Because' already shows the link, so 'so' is redundant.

quests.partialSentence: The manager who interviewed me ____.
options: who said the role was already filled
said the role was already filled
she said the role was already filled
saying the role was already filled
quests.correctAnswer: said the role was already filled
quests.hint: The subject needs a main verb.
quests.explanation: The relative clause is part of the subject; the main verb follows.

quests.partialSentence: The article that I ____ yesterday explains why prices keep rising.
quests.explanation: 'Yesterday' requires the simple past.

quests.partialSentence: While she was studying abroad, she ____ friends with people from many countries.
quests.hint: The main verb describes a result.
quests.explanation: Past simple for completed events.

quests.partialSentence: Unless we ____ the budget soon, we won't be able to hire anyone next year.
quests.explanation: Present simple in conditional clauses.
